title: Truth, austerity and the rest: renunciation surpasses them all
theme: Twelve answers to “what is highest” — truth, austerity, restraint, calm, giving, dharma, procreation, the fires, the agnihotra, sacrifice, mental worship — each with its adherents; renunciation, held by Brahmā, surpasses them all.

sandhi.type: t before l and before c
sandhi.rule: -t before l becomes l (P. 8.4.60 (तोर्लि)); -t before c becomes c (P. 8.4.40 (स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः)).

sandhi.type: t before a nasal; a + a
sandhi.rule: dānāt before n becomes dānān (P. 8.4.45 (यरोऽनुनासिकेऽनुनासिको वा)); na + ati- gives nāti- (P. 6.1.101 (अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः)).
The a of agnayaḥ is elided after the final e (P. 6.1.109 (एङः पदान्तादति)); agnayaḥ before the vowel of iti loses its visarga and stands in hiatus (agnaya iti).

samasa.meaning: those who live in the Veda (as students), celibates

morphology.note: The base, and the Tirupati e-text, print तमात्; the Ānandāśrama text reads तस्मात्, which the rest of the anuvāka uses in every other clause (‘therefore they delight in …’) and which both commentators read (Bhāskara: «तस्माच्छमे रमन्ते सर्वेऽपि»). The edition keeps the base and marks the place for review; the translation reads ‘therefore’.

A Vedic neuter plural of an s-stem paras- beside para- ‘high’; it stands in apposition to अवराणि: ‘these are lower — the (so-called) high ones’. Bhāskara’s text has तपांसि ‘austerities’ in this place.
Imperfect of the causative of ati-√ric ‘to exceed’: ‘made (them) left behind, surpassed’. The anonymous commentator glosses «अतिक्रान्तवान्».
A perfect form of √ah with present meaning: ‘says’. The one who says it is not named; the commentators supply a follower of the Veda («कश्चिद्वेदार्थपर आह»).

translation.literal: Truth [is] highest; the highest [is] truth. By truth they never fall from the heavenly world, for truth [is that] of the good; therefore they delight in truth. ‘Austerity’ [say others]: there is nothing higher than not eating; for what [is] the highest austerity, that [is] hard to bear, that [is] hard to overcome; therefore they delight in austerity. ‘Restraint’ [say] the celibate students, constantly; therefore they delight in restraint. ‘Calm’ [say] the sages in the forest; therefore they delight in calm. ‘Giving’: all beings praise [it]; nothing [is] harder to carry out than giving; therefore they delight in giving. ‘Dharma’: by dharma all this is held together; nothing [is] harder to do than dharma; therefore they delight in dharma. ‘Procreation’ [say] the many; therefore the greatest number beget offspring; therefore the greatest number delight in procreation. ‘The fires’, one says; therefore the fires are to be established. ‘The agnihotra’, one says; therefore they delight in the agnihotra. ‘Sacrifice’: for [by] sacrifice [are] the gods [in heaven]; therefore they delight in sacrifice. ‘The mental [worship]’ [say] the knowing; therefore the knowing delight only in the mental [worship]. ‘Renunciation’ [says] Brahmā; Brahmā indeed [is] highest, the highest indeed [is] Brahmā. These indeed are lower — the high ones; renunciation alone surpassed [them]. Who knows thus — this is the secret teaching.
translation.readable: Truth is the highest, say some: by truth no one falls from the heavenly world, for truth belongs to the good, and so they delight in truth. Others name austerity, for nothing is higher than fasting, and the highest austerity is hard to bear. The celibate students name restraint; the sages in the forest name calm. Giving is praised by all beings, and nothing is harder; dharma holds the whole world together; most people name procreation and have many children. One says the sacred fires, another the daily fire offering, others sacrifice, by which the gods reached heaven; the knowing delight in worship done in the mind. But Brahmā names renunciation — and Brahmā is the highest. All these others are lower; renunciation alone surpasses them. Whoever knows this has the secret teaching.

syntax: A catalogue of twelve short paragraphs built on one pattern: the name of a means, often marked by इति (‘“austerity”’), a reason in a nominal sentence or with हि, and the refrain तस्मात् … रमन्ते ‘therefore they delight in …’. The holders of each view are named in the nominative without a verb of saying (ब्रह्मचारिणः, मुनयः, भूयांसः, विद्वांसः, ब्रह्मा). The last paragraph turns the catalogue into a ranking: तानि … अवराणि … न्यास एवात्यरेचयत्, closed by the formula य एवं वेद … इत्युपनिषत्.

ambiguities.note: आह has no subject. The commentators supply a follower of the Veda for each view («कश्चिद्वेदार्थपर आह»); the text itself does not name one.

Literally ‘for sacrifice is the gods’. The anonymous commentator reads यज्ञः as an instrumental by Vedic interchange of cases and supplies ‘went to heaven’ («यज्ञो व्यत्ययेन तृतीया यज्ञेन»), matching 10.79’s यज्ञेन हि देवा दिवं गताः; Bhāskara calls the clause plain («यज्ञेन हीत्यादि स्पष्टम्»).

For the anonymous commentator and Sāyaṇa, Hiraṇyagarbha, who may be called the supreme because his knowledge equals it («परो हि परमात्मैव ब्रह्मा हिरण्यगर्भ इति वक्तुं शक्यते»). For Bhāskara, the one placed above all («ब्रह्मा हि सर्वस्मात् परम उपरि स्थितः»), and renunciation is in the place of Brahmā.

beginner: People have always disagreed about what matters most in life. This passage lists twelve answers. Some say truthfulness, because the truthful never fall. Some say austerity — above all fasting — because it is so hard. Students living under vows prize self-control; hermits in the forest prize a calm mind. Some prize generosity, some good works for the community, most people prize raising a family. Followers of the Vedic ritual prize keeping the sacred fires, the daily fire offering, or the great sacrifices; thoughtful people prize inner worship. Each group delights in its own answer. Then the passage gives its verdict: Brahmā, the creator, names renunciation — giving up the whole round of works — and all the other answers are lower than that. The next anuvāka tells the same teaching as a story.
analogy: Like a teacher who writes every student’s answer on the board, explains why each one is attractive, and only then circles the one answer that includes and surpasses the rest.

commentary.label: direct
commentary.text: It names twelve things held to be highest — truth, austerity, restraint, calm, giving, dharma, procreation, the fires, the agnihotra, sacrifice, mental worship and renunciation — gives a reason for each, and says that each has those who delight in it. It ends by calling the first eleven lower and saying that renunciation alone surpassed them.

commentary.q: Why does the list stand here?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: The anonymous commentator marks a new section, on renunciation, after the sections on food and on rites: «अथेदानीं सर्वकर्ममयसंसारबीजदाहार्थं संन्यासप्रकरणमारभ्यते» — renunciation, to burn the seed of the round of existence made of all works. To show that renunciation is the highest of the means to knowledge, the other eleven are set against it: «सत्यादीन्येकादशोत्कृष्टसाधनानि प्रतियोगित्वेन वक्तव्यानि». Sāyaṇa opens his comment with the same sentence.

commentary.q: How does each commentator read the list?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: For the anonymous commentator and Sāyaṇa, each item is someone’s view of the best means to release, with its adherents: «तपः परं मोक्षसाधनमिति केषांचिन्मतम्». Bhāskara reads the list as kinds of austerity (tapas), each held by some to be the highest, so that renunciation itself is the highest austerity: «सत्यादितपोव्युदासेन सन्न्यासाख्यस्य तपसः प्रकृष्टत्वं प्रतिपादगति»; for the second item he says «तप इति यत्प्रसिद्धं यमनियमादिकं तदेव परं तप इति पक्षान्तरम् इत्यर्थः». In support of truth he cites a verse: «अश्वमेधसहस्रं च सत्यं च तुलया धृतम्» — a thousand horse sacrifices weighed against truth — reported here as cited by him.

commentary.q: What is the renunciation meant here?
commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa: the giving up of the rites of the ritual portion of the Veda, such as the agnihotra, in the way the Āruṇi and Jābāla Upaniṣads teach — «पूर्वकाण्डोक्तानामग्निहोत्रादिकर्मणामारुणिजाबालाद्युपनिषदुक्तप्रकारेण परित्यागो न्यासः» — and it alone surpassed all the rest: «संन्यास एक एव तानि सर्वाण्यत्यरेचयत्». Bhāskara: the giving up of the fruit of all works — «सर्वकर्मफलत्यागो न्यासः स एव परमं तपः».

commentary.q: What does the text read at two doubtful places?
commentary.label: linguistic
commentary.text: In the sentence on calm the base and the Tirupati e-text print तमात्, the Ānandāśrama text तस्मात्; every other paragraph has तस्मात्, and the translation follows it. In the closing sentence the base reads एतान्यवराणि परांसि, ‘these are lower — the high ones’, while Bhāskara’s text reads तपांसि ‘austerities’ («तानि वा एतान्यवराणि तपांसि»); the edition keeps the base.

schools.disagreement: No Vedānta-school commentary on this text is in the edition’s sources (Raṅgarāmānuja’s is not among them): the anonymous bhāṣya, Sāyaṇa and Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara comment on the words and the rite. They differ on two points that matter here: whether the list is of means to release (the anonymous commentator, Sāyaṇa) or of kinds of austerity (Bhāskara), and whether ‘Brahmā’ is Hiraṇyagarbha (the anonymous commentator, Sāyaṇa) or the one placed above all (Bhāskara).

parallels.quote: सत्यमिति सत्यवचा राथीतरः । तप इति तपोनित्यः पौरुशिष्टिः
parallels.note: The Taittirīya Upaniṣad also names teachers who hold one thing — truth, austerity, recitation — to be the highest, in the same ‘X iti’ form; there the last word goes to recitation and teaching, here to renunciation.
The Bṛhadāraṇyaka names giving, sacrifice and austerity as ways the self is sought, and the wandering renunciants as those who seek it alone.

contemporary.text: Each group in the passage delights in the value it has chosen, and each has a good reason. The passage does not mock them; it ranks them. One can read it as a question about what one would keep if every other good had to be held loosely. This is a modern reflection, not part of the traditional reading.

reflect.beginner: Which of the twelve answers would you have given first, and why?
reflect.deeper: Why might a text praise each lower good before setting all of them below renunciation?
reflect.practice: Write down three things you value, and beside each the reason you would give for it.

references.text: Sāyaṇa’s comment on this anuvāka is his anuvāka 62; Bhāskara’s is his anuvāka 62. The anonymous commentator’s text follows Sāyaṇa’s almost word for word here.

flags.note: तमात् (base, Tirupati) against तस्मात् (Ānandāśrama): the collation lists it for review; the context and both commentators read तस्मात्.
परांसि (base) against तपांसि in Bhāskara’s text; and एवात्यरेचयद्य (base) against अत्यरेचयत् । य (Ānandāśrama, Tirupati), a review item that is a difference of pause only.

The other review items of the collation here are small: सुवर्गाल्लोकाच्च्यवन्ते (the Ānandāśrama text drops an ā; the Tirupati e-text reads लोहा-), and a visarga written in आधातव्याः before अग्निहोत्रम् by the Ānandāśrama and Tirupati texts (a difference of pause).
